import math

import torch


def grouped_query_attention(query, key, value, *, mask=None, causal=False):
    """GQA for Q(B,Hq,L,D), K/V(B,Hkv,S,D); Hkv=1 gives MQA.

    True in mask means allowed; mask must broadcast to (B,Hq,L,S).
    K/V heads are broadcast, never repeat_interleaved into a full copy.
    Score storage still costs O(B*Hq*L*S); this is not a fused kernel.
    """
    batch, query_heads, length, width = query.shape
    kv_heads = key.shape[1]
    if kv_heads <= 0 or query_heads % kv_heads or width <= 0:
        raise ValueError("positive KV heads must divide query heads")
    if key.shape != value.shape or key.shape[0] != batch or key.shape[-1] != width:
        raise ValueError("K/V must match and share Q's batch and head width")
    if key.shape[-2] == 0:
        raise ValueError("keys must be nonempty")
    groups = query_heads // kv_heads
    work_dtype = (
        torch.float32 if query.dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16) else query.dtype
    )
    grouped_queries = query.to(work_dtype).reshape(
        batch, kv_heads, groups, length, width
    )
    scores = grouped_queries @ key.to(work_dtype)[:, :, None].transpose(-2, -1)
    scores = scores.reshape(batch, query_heads, length, key.shape[-2]) / math.sqrt(
        width
    )
    allowed = torch.ones(scores.shape[-2:], dtype=torch.bool, device=query.device)
    if causal:
        allowed = allowed.tril()
    if mask is not None:
        if mask.dtype != torch.bool:
            raise ValueError("mask must be boolean")
        allowed = allowed & mask
    scores = scores.masked_fill(~allowed, -torch.inf)
    scores = torch.where(
        allowed.any(-1, keepdim=True), scores, torch.zeros_like(scores)
    )
    weights = scores.softmax(-1).masked_fill(~allowed, 0)
    weights = weights.reshape(batch, kv_heads, groups, length, key.shape[-2])
    context = weights @ value.to(work_dtype)[:, :, None]
    return context.reshape(batch, query_heads, length, width).to(value.dtype)

**The memory problem behind GQA.** During generation, every layer remembers keys and values for previous tokens. Standard multi-head attention stores a separate pair for every attention head. As the conversation grows, this cache becomes large and expensive to read for every new token. GQA reduces the number of distinct stored key/value heads while retaining multiple query heads. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13245)

**Use eight questioners and two reference books.** Think of eight query heads asking different questions, with each group of four consulting the same key/value “book.” The queries still differ, so their attention weights can differ even though they consult shared keys and values. With eight query heads and two KV heads, cache storage for K/V is one quarter of the eight-KV-head version, assuming equal head width and precision.

MQA is the extreme case: all query heads share one KV head. MHA is the other extreme: every query head has its own KV head. GQA lies between them and offers a quality–memory tradeoff rather than a free mathematical equivalence to MHA.

**Implement the grouping explicitly.** Reshape query heads into a KV-head axis and a group axis. For $H_q=8,H_{kv}=2$, each key/value head broadcasts across four query heads. The number of query heads must be divisible by the KV-head count under this simple grouping convention. Keep the head ordering consistent through concatenation and output projection.

**A common misconception in the prompt.** `repeat_interleave` repeats tensor values and ordinarily allocates expanded storage; it is not itself a memory-free broadcast. Broadcasting can avoid storing repeated K/V, but the attention score tensor may still be large. Check the actual kernel and allocated memory. Cache savings, intermediate-score savings, and arithmetic savings are three different measurements.

**Technical details and references.**

Group consecutive query heads around each shared KV head. Keeping a separate group axis lets batched matmul broadcast K/V without making a repeated KV tensor. Hkv=1 is MQA; Hkv=Hq is MHA. KV-cache storage scales with Hkv, but the number of query attention distributions still scales with Hq. repeat_interleave creates repeated values; it does not by itself avoid the memory copy. The reference still materializes scores and is not a fused GPU implementation.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** KV storage is $2BLSH_{kv}d_hb$ bytes for batch $B$, layers $L$, sequence length $S$, and $b$ bytes per element. Reducing KV heads from $H_q$ to $H_{kv}$ reduces that storage in the same ratio. Query heads remain distinct, so sharing KV heads does not collapse all heads to one attention distribution. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13245)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://aiexpjourney.substack.com/p/grouped-query-attention-gqa-explained-5f3dbbfe013b) and [2](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention.html).
